clue.text: Washington state put into new redrafts later

indicators.note: something made new is reshaped, so the following word's letters are rearranged
one item is placed inside another, so the state goes within the reworked word

blocks.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An American state is written into fresh drafts of a document at a later stage.
explanation.walkthrough: REDRAFTS is rearranged as AFTER_RDS and WA slips into the gap to make AFTERWARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Confidence in football authorities — just what's needed before end of match

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body
'just the thing' or 'it' in the sense of exactly what is wanted
the last letter of match

explanation.surface: A fan says confidence in the football bosses is just the thing needed as the game closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's IT' is said of exactly what was wanted. 'Before' just places IT ahead of the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith is trust or belief, a synonym for confidence.

clue.text: English rental changes — unceasing

indicators.note: the word that changes has its letters altered in order

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that English rents keep changing without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting for ever, without stopping, as unceasing does.

clue.text: Women's home triumph

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A women's team celebrates a victory on their own ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A win is a victory, the same thing as a triumph.

clue.text: Hardy note, not saying anything about one

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the silent word wraps round the numeral

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
someone silent says nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A note from the novelist Hardy that says nothing about a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H suggests Thomas Hardy the novelist; it is the adjective hardy, meaning tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy plant or person is tough and able to withstand difficulty, which is what resilient means.

clue.text: Do wrong, securing cheers — black mark?

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: to sin is to do wrong
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether misbehaving while earning applause leaves a black mark on their record.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta and cheers are both casual British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on a reputation is a figurative blemish, the same as a black mark against someone.

clue.text: Discuss river providing home for nocturnal creature

indicators.note: giving something a home means housing it, so the river surrounds the creature

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a bat is a flying mammal active at night

explanation.surface: An instruction to talk about how a river shelters some night animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee flows through Wales, England and Scotland and is a favourite crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a matter is to argue it out formally, so the verb is a synonym of discuss.

clue.text: Flier, professional, is good example of nervelessness, first of all

indicators.note: the first of all of the words means taking the opening letter of each one in turn

blocks.clueFragment: professional, is good example of nervelessness
blocks.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A daring pilot, a pro, is held up as a model of fearlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an aviator, but the flier is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon is a bird that flies, so it is a flier in the most literal sense.

clue.text: Having embraced husband, one putting money away for electric device

indicators.note: something that has embraced another holds it within its arms, so the saver wraps round the letter

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
a person who saves money

explanation.surface: After hugging her husband, a thrifty woman puts money aside for an electrical gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric shaver is a powered appliance for shaving, so it is an example of an electric device.

clue.text: Feature of country? Not entirely

indicators.note: not the entire word means part of it is cut away, here its final letter

blocks.note: China is a country in Asia

explanation.surface: A question about some feature of a country, answered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature of country' looks like a landscape feature; it is a facial feature, and CHINA loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Features are parts of the face, and the chin is one of them.

clue.text: Source of timely information from local: end argument?

indicators.note: coming from the words that follow means drawn out of them, as a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: A local resident hopes a reliable source of information will settle a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across loCAL ENDARgument.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar tells you dates and days, so it is a source of information about time.

clue.text: Agreement counts, regularly forgotten, must be included in population survey

indicators.note: losing letters at regular intervals means every other one goes, leaving the alternate ones
to be included in something means to sit inside it, so the kept letters go within the survey

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters, the others being dropped
a census is an official count of a population

explanation.surface: A consensus that counts left out of a census must be put back in.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general agreement reached among a group.

clue.text: Hot German bread, with centre removed

indicators.note: removing the centre of a word takes out its middle letter

blocks.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: A warm German loaf served with its middle cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' looks like a description of the bread, but it is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen, as with goods too recently taken to sell openly.

clue.text: Part of seasonal meal flop

blocks.note: first meaning: the bird roasted for Christmas dinner
second meaning: a failed show or film

explanation.walkthrough: The word is both the Christmas bird and slang for a theatrical or film failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast bird is the centrepiece of a festive dinner, and a failure on stage or screen is called a turkey.

clue.text: Former Queen welcoming composer's cash cow

indicators.note: someone welcoming a guest takes them in, so the queen surrounds the composer

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, refers to the late Queen Elizabeth II
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A former monarch welcomes a composer whose work makes good money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is only part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is something that brings in money, which is what a cash cow is.

clue.text: Literary genre referring to some languages

blocks.note: first meaning: a love story or tale of adventure
second meaning: describing the languages descended from Latin

explanation.definitionFit: Romance is a fiction genre, and the Romance languages, such as French and Spanish, come from Latin.

clue.text: Look for gold maybe chance of success

blocks.note: first meaning: to search the ground for minerals
second meaning: the likelihood of something happening

explanation.definitionFit: Miners prospect for gold or oil, and a prospect is also a possibility of future success.

clue.text: Son went to move fast

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
peed means urinated, informally went to the toilet

explanation.surface: A son nipped off quickly, as children do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is a euphemism for urinating, so it gives PEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed is to go quickly, the same as moving fast.

clue.text: Horse's unpleasant experience

blocks.note: first meaning: a female horse
second meaning: British slang, short for nightmare

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is'. In British slang a mare is a nightmare, a terrible time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is a female horse, and in British colloquial speech a bad experience is 'a right mare'.

clue.text: Source of remote Russian river, characteristic of the country

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of remote
the Ural flows from Russia's Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: The source of a far-off Russian river lies in typical countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things belonging to the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: Referring to Church, Saints, in break

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in letters
CE is the Church of England
SS is the abbreviation for saints

explanation.surface: Talk of the Church and the saints comes up during a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break from work, as when Parliament or a court adjourns.

clue.text: Glad rags? Well, extremely ritzy!

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

blocks.note: being fine means being well
the first and last letters of ritzy

explanation.surface: Someone eyes another's party outfit and remarks how very swanky it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for ritzy but asks for its outer letters. Glad rags are one's best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Finery is elaborate, showy clothing, which is what glad rags are.

clue.text: Company failing to complete large plant

indicators.note: not completing a word means stopping before its final letter

blocks.note: a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A company has gone bust before finishing a big factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large plant' suggests an industrial plant, but it means a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir is a coniferous tree, and a tree is a large plant.

clue.text: Old dryer is wrecked, unmanageable

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken-down old tumble dryer has become impossible to control.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means unruly or out of control, which is what unmanageable conveys.
